item.title: AI Revolution vs. Computing Revolution (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: I have been reading a lot about computing revolution in 60s/70s. Seeing a lot of parallels to today. A bunch of enterprises spent millions on these IBM/DEC machines but didn't see any ROI. But then a lot of consulting and product companies popped up to help with that. IBM/DEC had crazy high margins during this time (similar to Nvidia/micron etc) but all withered away eventually. In the end the software companies (Microsoft, Google etc.) captured most of the value, what's the equivalent of that for AI? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50120075 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

item.title: Show HN: Agent Chat in Your Markdown Notes - Chat with Context and Save Response (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: EtherPK now has Agent Chat. I use AI agents in two distinct ways. For coding I use TUIs, but for day-to-day and non code projects I used to use the web chat UIs like many others. Two things about this was always jarring: You're starting context from scratch. You might have a couple of agent instructions configured, but you have to tell the agent what you're thinking, from the beginning. When you get the information you need, holding on to it is hard. Within a day or two it's burried in your chat history. EtherPK is a mardown based PKMS (notes app), and it solves both of these problems. You can type /Agent within your notes (EtherPK supports standard prose and outliner blocks in the same document). The Agent Chat panel opens within your document, and you can choose how much context to give it. That might be nothing, the current block tree, the document or the whole graph (in the case of the latter - immediate surounding context is sent and the agent is given tools to navigate the rest of your graph). You control what the agent gets, and what stays private. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50119958 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
